content: In France, public hospitals fully cover prenatal and postnatal care through the social security system. Employed women receive 16 weeks of maternity leave, with daily pay ranging roughly from €9.29 to €84.90 depending on prior earnings. Financially, pregnancy and the weeks around childbirth generally don’t create extra hardship beyond existing conditions: economically vulnerable families remain strained, while wealthier ones stay comfortable. But practical support for new mothers is limited — paternity leave is just 11 days, barely allowing time for maternal recovery. New mothers therefore must cope with constant caregiving demands while healing and also find childcare, despite state-provided places being insufficient, particularly around Paris. Childcare costs vary: in municipal daycare the poorest households might pay about €1,000 a year, yet there is only one place for every eight children, so many turn to private solutions like childminders or in-home care. Any other questions?
